frames.heading: How to sit this practice exam

lines.say: This exam covers all of BIO1022. Most marks come from applying ideas to data.
Two hours, closed book. About 40 minutes for multiple choice, 80 for short answers.

draw.alt: Time split: 40 minutes MCQ, 80 minutes short answer

lines.say: Write your short answers on paper first, before reading the solutions.
Evaluate means judge strengths and weaknesses. Calculate means show every step and units.
The blastopore becomes the mouth. So it's a protostome.
A cavity fully lined by mesoderm is a true coelom.
Jointed legs and a moulted cuticle. That's Arthropoda, in the Ecdysozoa.

draw.alt: Decision path from bilateral to protostome to Ecdysozoa to Arthropoda

lines.say: Freshwater fish gain water by osmosis, so they make lots of dilute urine.
Birds excrete uric acid. It's non-toxic, nearly insoluble, and costs little water.
lines.write: uric acid: low water, safe in egg

lines.say: At 10 degrees, a mouse uses about five times more oxygen per gram than a lizard.
The mouse is an endotherm, making heat to stay near 37. The lizard just cools down.

draw.alt: Mouse stays at 37 degrees using lots of oxygen; lizard cools to 10 degrees

items.text: heat made by metabolism costs O₂

lines.say: 60 rabbits, r is 0.6, for 4 years. 60 times e to the 2.4.
That's 60 times 11.02. About 661 rabbits.
Logistic growth at 1500: 0.6 times 1500, times 500 over 2000.
That's 225 rabbits per year.
Growth is fastest at half of K, which is 1000. The rate is r K over 4, so 300.

draw.alt: S-shaped logistic curve with steepest point at K/2

lines.say: Drought kills 40 percent at any density. Disease spreads faster when crowded.
More toxic newts go with more resistant snakes. A positive correlation.
Each side selects the other. That's an arms race. Region C is a hotspot.
But correlation isn't cause. Show resistance is heritable to make the case.
R nought is 4. The herd immunity threshold is 1 minus a quarter.
So 75 percent of people must be immune.
Neutralising antibodies block the virus from attaching to host cell receptors.
The first dose makes memory cells. The second dose triggers a faster, bigger response.
Lose helper T cells, and B cells can't be activated. Antibodies fall.

draw.alt: Helper T cell removed: B cells and cytotoxic T cells lose activation

lines.say: Cytotoxic T cells also need helper cytokines, so infected cells survive longer.
Innate defences, like skin, phagocytes and NK cells, still work. They don't need T cells.
